sections.html: The African Butterfly fish, Pantodon buchholzi, becomes about 10 cm long. It is a strictly surface-dwelling species. Males can be easily recognized by the modified anal fin.
The specimens kept by the authors originate from Nigeria.
In the wild, it lives in quite shallow water of swamps.

Butterfly fishes are peaceful against other fish, but they tend to be a bit anxious. It is recommended to keep them only with very calm and peaceful fish. Against conspecifics Butterfly fishes can be quarrelsome, but this behaviour is usually only evanescent.

Pantodon can really fly, he is a glider. The Butterfly fish is a strictly surface-dwelling species. The ventral fins are modified to sensitive organs that help the fish to orient. Pantodon can survive in almost oxygen-free water due to a special organ that allows the fish to breathe air that is swallowed from the water surface.
Males can be easily recognized by the modified anal fin.
Butterfly fishes often spawn in aquaria, but the offspring is difficult to rear, because the larvae feed exclusively from the water surface – like their parents do.

There is a legend that says Pantodon was not discovered by an ichthyologist, but by a collector of butterflies. This collector caught Pantodon during a flight and thought initially the fish would be a moth.
